definition: IT security architecture is the design of controls, trust boundaries and system relationships to protect information and technology assets.
example: An architect isolates a payment service on its own network and restricts which services may contact it.

definition: IT security documentation is the creation and maintenance of written records that describe security requirements, controls, procedures and decisions.
example: A team documents who approves privileged access and how the approvals are recorded.

definition: ITU-T T.30 is the recommendation governing call setup, negotiation and message transfer for Group 3 facsimile over the telephone network.
example: Two fax machines use its signaling procedures to agree on how to send a page.

definition: Ivalua is enterprise software that supports sourcing, supplier management, purchasing and other source-to-pay activities.
example: A procurement team compares supplier bids before sending the selected contract for approval.

definition: JaCoCo is a Java code-coverage library that records which parts of compiled code run during tests.
example: A developer uses its branch report to find an unchecked path in a validation method.

definition: JacORB is a Java implementation of the CORBA object request broker architecture for distributed object communication.
example: A Java client uses JacORB to invoke an operation on a remote CORBA object.

definition: JAFAN refers to a family of U.S. Air Force and joint publications for administering and protecting special access programs.
example: A program security officer checks which manual applies when reviewing facility requirements.
sense_note: The label does not identify a particular JAFAN document or revision; applicability should be verified.

definition: Jasmine is a JavaScript testing framework that specifies expected behavior through test cases and assertions.
example: A developer writes a Jasmine test to check that a sorting function returns results in ascending order.

definition: The Java Archive format packages Java classes and related resources in a ZIP-based file that can contain a manifest.
example: A build packages a command-line application and its resources in a JAR with a declared entry point.

definition: The Java Communications API defines Java interfaces for accessing serial and parallel communication ports.
example: A desktop application opens a serial port to read data from an attached instrument.

definition: Java Persistence API 2.0 specifies object-relational mapping and persistence for Java applications, including entity management and type-safe criteria queries.
example: A service uses an entity manager to load a customer stored in a relational table.

definition: A JavaScript engine parses and executes JavaScript programs, often compiling code or using intermediate instructions internally.
example: A browser uses its engine to execute an event handler when a user clicks a button.

definition: JavaScriptCore is WebKit's engine for executing JavaScript code.
example: A WebKit-based application evaluates page scripts using JavaScriptCore.

definition: JavaServer Faces 2.0 is a Java specification for constructing server-side web interfaces from reusable components with a defined request lifecycle.
example: A web form uses Facelets and JSF components to display validation errors after submission.

definition: JAX-RPC is an older Java API for invoking remote procedures using XML-based web services, commonly with SOAP.
example: A legacy Java client calls a published SOAP operation through a generated stub.

definition: JAX-WS is a Java API for building and consuming XML-based web services, including SOAP services.
example: A programmer binds a Java service method to a SOAP endpoint described by WSDL.

definition: JD Edwards CNC is the administration discipline for installing, configuring and operating the JD Edwards EnterpriseOne technical environment.
example: An administrator builds and deploys an EnterpriseOne application package to a test environment.

definition: JdbcTemplate is a Spring Framework class that simplifies Java database access by managing JDBC resources and repetitive query code.
example: A service uses JdbcTemplate to execute a parameterized query and map the returned rows.

definition: JDesktop Network Components refers to Java components intended to simplify access to networked services and data from desktop applications.
example: A desktop application uses a data provider to display results obtained from a remote service.

definition: Jersey is a Java framework that implements the JAX-RS API for developing RESTful services and clients.
example: A Java service uses Jersey to route an HTTP GET request to an annotated resource method.

definition: Jive Software refers to enterprise collaboration software that supports communities, discussions and shared documents.
example: An organization uses a Jive community to publish reference documents and answer employee questions.
sense_note: The label could name the company rather than its collaboration product.

definition: jMock is a Java testing library that verifies interactions between code under test and simulated dependencies.
example: A test checks that a billing service invokes its mocked payment gateway exactly once.

definition: JMockit is a Java testing library for substituting dependencies and verifying interactions in unit tests.
example: A test replaces a clock dependency so it can verify expiration behavior using a fixed time.

definition: Job scheduling is the coordination of when tasks run, including their triggers, dependencies, resource availability and recurrence.
example: An operations team runs a reporting job only after the nightly data import completes.

definition: Joint Clearance and Access Verification System was an interface within the U.S. Department of Defense personnel security system for recording and verifying clearance and access information.
example: A security office used JCAVS to check personnel eligibility before processing requests for access.
sense_note: Historical system; do not infer current availability from the name.

definition: Joint Commission standards set accreditation requirements for health care organizations' quality, safety and operational practices.
example: A hospital reviews medication management practices against the requirements that apply to its accreditation program.

definition: JointJS is a JavaScript library for displaying and editing interactive diagrams made from elements and links.
example: A web application uses JointJS to let users connect workflow steps visually.

definition: Joomla is a content management system for publishing and administering websites through configurable templates and extensions.
example: A nonprofit site editor uses Joomla to publish an article without editing the site's HTML.

definition: JPEG is a set of coding standards for compressing continuous-tone digital images, most commonly used with lossy compression.
example: A photographer saves a smaller web copy of a camera image as a JPEG.

definition: JSData is a JavaScript data-management library that provides records, relationships and adapters for application data.
example: A developer defines a record type and uses a REST adapter to load it from a server.

definition: JSFiddle is a browser-based editor for combining and sharing runnable HTML, CSS and JavaScript examples.
example: A developer shares a small JSFiddle to demonstrate how a browser layout behaves.

definition: jsGrid is a JavaScript data-grid component for presenting and manipulating table records in a browser.
example: An admin page uses jsGrid to show a sortable inventory table with editable quantities.

definition: JSON Web Token is a compact format for transmitting claims as a JSON object, commonly signed or integrity-protected with JWS or encrypted with JWE.
example: An API verifies a signed token's issuer, audience and expiration before accepting its claims.

definition: jsPerf is a browser-based JavaScript benchmarking tool for comparing the execution rates of code snippets under its test harness.
example: A developer creates a benchmark to compare two array-processing expressions in the same browser.

definition: JsRender is a JavaScript templating library that renders templates against data to produce text or HTML.
example: A page renders one product row for each item in an array using a JsRender template.

definition: JsUnit is a JavaScript unit-testing framework modeled on the xUnit family of test frameworks.
example: A developer uses a JsUnit assertion to verify the result of a date-formatting function.
sense_note: Multiple historical projects used similar capitalization; confirm the implementation if product-specific detail is needed.

definition: JTrac is a web-based issue tracker for recording and organizing work items.
example: A support team records a defect in JTrac and assigns it to a developer.

definition: Jury instructions are the court's directions explaining the law, issues and legal standards jurors must apply in deciding a case.
example: A judge explains the applicable burden of proof to jurors before deliberations.
sense_note: The skill interpretation is preparing or communicating the instructions; the label itself names the instructions.

definition: Jury management is the administration of jury service, including summonses, attendance, availability and assignment of jurors.
example: A court office schedules jurors and tracks which panels are available for trials.

definition: Juvenile rehabilitation supports young people involved in the justice system in changing behavior and returning safely to their communities.
example: A caseworker coordinates counseling, school attendance and reentry support for a youth leaving placement.
